definitions.gloss: earthen or concrete floor at a Japanese entrance
definitions.explanation: The hard-floored lower area at the entrance of a Japanese house (genkan) where shoes are removed. Originally made by pounding a mixture of earth, lime, and bittern, now typically concrete or tile.

examples.japanese: {三和土|たたき}で{靴|くつ}を{脱|ぬ}ぐ。
examples.english: To take off shoes on the entrance floor.

examples.japanese: {三和土|たたき}が{汚|よご}れていたので、{掃除|そうじ}した。
examples.english: The entrance floor was dirty, so I cleaned it.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{民家|みんか}の{三和土|たたき}は{土|つち}を{固|かた}めて{作|つく}られている。
examples.english: The entrance floors of old traditional houses are made of compacted earth.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
The word {三和土|たたき} comes from the process of making the floor: three materials ({土|つち}, {石灰|せっかい}, and にがり) were mixed and pounded (たたく) to create a hard surface. The kanji {三和土|さんわど} literally means "three-mixed earth."

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {三和土|たたき} is the lowest level of the {玄関|げんかん} (entrance). Visitors step up from the {三和土|たたき} onto the raised floor ({上|あ}がり{框|がまち}) when entering the house. In modern homes, the {三和土|たたき} is usually tiled or made of concrete.

NOTE:
Not to be confused with たたき as in {鰹|かつお}のたたき (seared bonito), which is a different word.
